harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as a router between two previously-unconfigured L2 segments (lan-a on vtnet1/opt1, lan-b on vtnet2/opt2), with static addressing on node2 (10.50.10.11) and node3 (10.50.20.12). Added a manual/hybrid outbound NAT rule scoped to source 10.50.10.0/24 egressing on opt2, so node2→node3 connections arrive at node3 SNAT'd to node1's lan-b address (10.50.20.1), while node3→node2 connections retain node3's real source address (verified via tcpdump on node1's opt2/opt1 interfaces and by observing the peer's addr on each side). Completed the mandatory sequential single-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node1 via `shutdown -r now`, node2/node3 via `reboot`), confirming boot-identity change on each (FreeBSD kern.boottime; Linux boot_id) and re-verifying post-restart that OPNsense's interface/NAT config persisted from config.xml and that the asymmetric-NAT behavior still functions end-to-end after all three restarts.
actions_performed: Discovered actual L2 topology via tcpdump/STP frames: vtnet1=lan-a (paired with node2 enp8s0), vtnet2=lan-b (paired with node3 enp8s0); both were admin-down and had to be brought up
Assigned persistent static IPs via systemd-networkd drop-in files on node2 (10.50.10.11/24) and node3 (10.50.20.12/24), plus static routes to the peer subnet via node1

Edited node1's /conf/config.xml (with backups) via Python/ElementTree to add opt1 (LANA, 10.50.10.1/24) and opt2 (LANB, 10.50.20.1/24) interfaces, pass firewall rules for opt1<->opt2, and a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule SNATing 10.50.10.0/24 to the opt2 interface address

Applied config via configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2 and configctl filter reload; fixed an initial NAT rule schema mistake (plain-text source vs required nested <address> element) discovered by inspecting OPNsense's SNatRule/Rule PHP source and pfctl -s nat output
Verified asymmetric NAT with live TCP connections captured via tcpdump: node2->node3 arrives as 10.50.20.1 (node1's lan-b addr); node3->node2 arrives as node3's real 10.50.20.12

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, node3: captured baseline boot identity/service health, issued native reboot (shutdown -r now on FreeBSD, reboot on Ubuntu) with backgrounded non-blocking acknowledgement, polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot identity (kern.boottime / boot_id), and re-verified interface config, NAT rules, and full connection-level asymmetric-NAT behavior after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b (topology discovery and interface configuration)
evidence.summary: Identified vtnet1/vtnet2 as unbridged-but-down interfaces paired to node2/node3 via STP+ARP capture, brought them up, and configured them as OPNsense opt1 (LANA 10.50.10.1/24) and opt2 (LANB 10.50.20.1/24)

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 addressed on separate lan-a/lan-b subnets with mutual routes
evidence.summary: Static systemd-networkd config applied: node2=10.50.10.11/24 with route to 10.50.20.0/24 via node1; node3=10.50.20.12/24 with route to 10.50.10.0/24 via node1

evidence.requirement: node2->node3 connection observed by node3 as arriving from a node1 address (not node2's own)
evidence.summary: pfctl -s nat shows the scoped SNAT rule (from 10.50.10.0/24 to any -> (vtnet2:0)); live TCP capture on node1's vtnet2 shows the SYN arriving from 10.50.20.1 (node1's lan-b address), and node3's nc server received the payload

evidence.requirement: node3->node2 connection (reverse direction) keeps its original source address
evidence.summary: Live TCP capture on node1's vtnet1 during a node3->node2 connection shows the SYN retaining node3's real source address 10.50.20.12, confirming no NAT applied in that direction

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered NAT/interface state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=17:56:46 captured; shutdown -r now acknowledged and returned before disconnect; SSH timed out during reboot; post-reboot kern.boottime=18:04:31 proves restart; opt1/opt2 interfaces and the scoped outbound NAT rule persisted from config.xml, and a fresh TCP connection post-reboot showed SNAT still applying correctly

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered network/data state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=df9e2dce...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; exec timed out during reboot; post-reboot boot_id=d0eb619a... (changed) with new uptime; static IP/route on enp8s0 persisted and ping to node3 across the router succeeded

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered network/data state, and full asymmetric-NAT behavior confirmed after all three restarts
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=37344ae4...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; exec timed out during reboot; post-reboot boot_id=2f3ae971... (changed) with new uptime; static IP/route persisted; final end-to-end TCP test after all three nodes were restarted shows node2->node3 still arrives as 10.50.20.1 (SNAT intact) and node3 received the payload
